content.text: I am thinking about adding a quarkus dev-ui for pathland. What could be intersting to expose there?
I'll explore the Quarkus extension and server runtime to ground the ideas in what Pathland actually exposes.

1: # pathland-quarkus — implementation status
2: 
3: **Last updated:** November 7, 2026
4: 
5: Quarkus extension for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each
6: app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding this extension + a
7: `PathlandApp` CDI bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at
8: their own subpaths (the BFF layout). Author the root view with
9: `pathland-view-core`'s Kotlin DSL; Java hosts return Kotlin views from a
10: `PathlandApp` bean. The extension also provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus.kotlin`
11: capability and pulls in `quarkus-kotlin`.
12: 
13: ## Implemented
14: 
15: - **Security defaults (issue #63)**: the deployment module contributes
16:   overridable runtime defaults via `RunTimeConfigurationDefaultBuildItem`:
17:   `quarkus.http.cors.enabled=true` (no origins → same-origin, which covers
18:   WebSocket upgrades because the CORS filter runs before routes),
19:   `quarkus.websockets-next.server.max-message-size`/`max-frame-size=65536`, and
20:   CSP + `X-Content-Type-Options`/`Referrer-Policy`/`X-Frame-Options` headers via
21:   `quarkus.http.header.*`. See `docs/HARDENING.md` for overrides, CSP rollout,
22:   reverse-proxy/TLS guidance, and edge rate limiting. The `wid` handshake query
23:   is validated by server-core (`WindowIds`). **HSTS is deliberately not an
24:   extension default** — it is a whole-origin, persistent browser policy that
25:   also covers other apps on the same server, so it is owned by the application
26:   or edge; the Quarkus demo opts in via `application.properties`.
27:   `docs/HARDENING.md` documents the directives and override guidance.
28: - **Hosted deployments work by default**: the same defaults set
29:   `quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding`, `allow-x-forwarded`, and
30:   `enable-forwarded-host` to `true`, so a TLS-terminating PaaS (Render, Fly,
31:   Heroku, Cloud Run) gets a correct same-origin WebSocket check and an external
32:   SSR canonical URL with zero configuration. These are lowest-priority defaults;
33:   application config (including
34:   `quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding=false`) always wins.
35: - **Topic hub bean**: the extension produces a `PathlandSignalHub` singleton
36:   (`host.signalHub()`: root mount, else the first mount) for external UI updates.
37:   `TopicSubscriptionsTest` mounts a `/topics` app and proves a background-thread
38:   publish reaches only the session subscribed for that subject.
39: - **Java host / Kotlin views**: `CounterApp` is a Java CDI bean whose
40:   `newRoot()` returns a Kotlin-authored fixture view; the multi-session
41:   WebSocket tests prove SSR + live deltas work through that mount.
42: 
43: - **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt.
44: - **SEO document head (issue #45)**: `IndexResource` derives the canonical URL
45:   from `UriInfo` and passes host-default `PageMetadata` to the registry;
46:   `PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...)` may override it per route before the first
47:   paint. Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are on by default and configurable via
48:   `pathland.seo.{enabled,site-name,image,og-type,twitter-card,twitter-site,structured-data}`.
49: 
50: - **`PathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/_pathland/ws")` for the root app: 1:1 sessions
51:   per connection (a fresh `uiId` per connection + the client's `wid` state scope from
52:   the `?wid=` query param), binary events routed into the root registry of the
53:   `PathlandHost`. **Stateless (critical)**: quarkus-websockets-next endpoints default
54:   to `@Singleton` — one shared instance for all connections — so the per-connection
55:   ids come from `connection.id()` + the handshake and the `QuarkusConnection` adapters
56:   live in a map keyed by connection id. Memoizing `uiId`/`wid`/`transport` on the
57:   shared instance collapsed every connection onto ONE session (multiple browsers shared
58:   one UI model — a probe or second tab drove the first tab's session).
59: - **`MountedPathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/{app}/_pathland/ws")` for mounted apps:
60:   the `{app}` path param resolves the app's registry. Mount paths are single-segment.
61:   Same stateless rule as the root socket.
62: - **`IndexResource`** — JAX-RS SSR catch-all (`/` + deep links; `/_pathland/**` and the
63:   Quarkus non-application root `/q/**` — health/metrics — excluded via negative lookahead)
64:   dispatching to the longest-mount app (prefix stripped);
65:   SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS);
66:   per-app framework files (`/{app}/_pathland/...`, e.g. the mounted app's bundle) are
67:   served from the shared `/_pathland/**` classpath mount. Quarkus serves the global
68:   `/_pathland/**` bundle + asset mount from `META-INF/resources` before JAX-RS.
69:   **The extension jar ships the DOM client bundle** (`META-INF/resources/_pathland/
70:   dom-renderer-<hash>.js` + the `dom-renderer.current` pointer + the service worker), so
71:   a consuming application adds the extension and needs no static resources of its own;
72:   the mounted-base `frameworkFile` path resolves the app's classpath copy first (TCCL),
73:   then the extension jar, and adds `immutable` caching for the content-hashed bundle. A
74:   `/_pathland/{file}` JAX-RS route is a fallback for deployments where Quarkus's static
75:   handler is unavailable (it normally wins).
76:   **`/_pathland/{name}.css`** (global JAX-RS route + the mounted-base
77:   `frameworkFile` path) serves the renderer-owned content-hashed base design
78:   (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
79:   `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. **`/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg`**
80:   serves the renderer-owned icon glyphs from the shared Rust renderer
81:   (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` → `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache
82:   header — no static CSS/icon files on any host. SSR links the CSS via
83:   `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.
84: - **`PathlandRegistryProducer`** — CDI `@Produces @Singleton` `PathlandHost` from every
85:   `MountedApp` bean plus the lone `PathlandApp` bean (mounted at `/`); `@Disposes` shuts
86:   it down. Reads the `pathland.debug-html` config property (default `false`) to enable
87:   per-node HTML comments in SSR output, and `pathland.service-worker` (default `false`)
88:   to opt the DOM client into the per-window-id service worker (issue #155) — served at
89:   `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
90: - **`ServiceWorkerFilter`** — serves `/_pathland/sw.js` (root and mounted bases) with
91:   `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so the client's root-scoped
92:   registration succeeds. A `Filters` handler always runs before routes, so it wins over
93:   Quarkus's static-resource handler (which sends neither header, and whose configured
94:   max-age would otherwise cache the script and delay update detection). The script is
95:   resolved through the thread-context classloader first, then the extension's own
96:   loader, then the system loader: extension runtime classes live in Quarkus's base
97:   runtime classloader and cannot see the application's `META-INF/resources` copy. The
98:   extension jar bundles the worker as a fallback (the TS copy script writes it), and
99:   `pathland-quarkus-demo`'s integration test asserts the headers on both the root and a
100:   mounted base — the packaged-app classloader path the module-local test could not see.
101: - **Observability (issue #62)** — `quarkus-micrometer` (a `MeterRegistry` bean) +
102:   `quarkus-smallrye-health`: the producer builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over the
103:   registry and decorates it with `TracingTelemetry` when a `Tracer` bean is present and
104:   `quarkus.otel.enabled` (default `true`; the extension never touches the OTel API when
105:   the extension is absent/disabled). `PathlandHealthCheck` (`@Readiness`) reports the
106:   host UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/q/health`; the `pathland.*` meters appear
107:   at `/q/metrics`.
108: - **`QuarkusConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketConnection` to `PathlandConnection`.
109:   Sends are **serialized** (one `sendBinary` subscription in flight, the rest queued),
110:   and a **send failure closes the connection** so the session drops it and the DOM
111:   client reconnects + `META::RESYNC` (recoverable) instead of silently stalling on an
112:   "open" socket that never delivers (the remote seekbar symptom). **Send timeout**: a
113:   `sendBinary` that neither completes nor fails within 10 s (a half-dead connection /
114:   a dropped proxy upstream leg) is marked failed and closed — a hung send would
115:   otherwise wedge the serialized drain forever. **Keep-alive pings**: the connection
116:   sends a WS-protocol ping every 15 s (browsers auto-pong) to keep the connection warm
117:   through middleboxes and detect a dead client; `close()` stops the keep-alive
118:   scheduler (the sockets' `@OnClose` calls it).
119: - **Heartbeat** — both sockets reply to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
120:   **at the transport layer** (through their `QuarkusConnection`, no actor/session
121:   dependency, and a PING never creates or wakes a session); spec/OPCODE.md
122:   §Transport heartbeat.
123: - **Failure handling** — `fail()` logs the reason; `close()` (socket `@OnClose`)
124:   no longer calls `close()` on the already-closed connection (no spurious
125:   "Connection already closed" noise). A **transient write failure on a connection
126:   that still reports open is logged, not closed** — only a confirmed-dead channel
127:   (or a send hung past the timeout) warrants closing. The send-timeout task is
128:   **cancelled when the send completes**, so a completed-but-late callback can't
129:   false-time-out and kill a healthy connection. Keep-alive pings are sent directly
130:   (Vert.x serializes writes — no sync with `sendBinary` needed).
131: - `META-INF/beans.xml` so Quarkus discovers the extension.
132: - **Native image support** — the deployment module registers the renderer-owned
133:   `dev/pathland/render/html/base.css` + `.name` resources via
134:   `NativeImageResourceBuildItem`, so `HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` works in a GraalVM
135:   native executable without app-level `quarkus.native.resources.includes`.
136:   JNA is not on the server classpath (the ring interop lives in
137:   `pathland-native-core`), and Redis/Lettuce is opt-in via
138:   `pathland-state-redis`, so the demo's native image carries neither.
139:   The demo's Dockerfile builds with the Mandrel 25 builder image and runs the
140:   resulting executable on the UBI9 Quarkus micro image.
141: - **Quarkus extension metadata** — runtime + `pathland-quarkus-deployment`; the
142:   runtime provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus` capability. The runtime has no
143:   dependency on the authoring DSL. Tests use Kotlin-authored fixture views to prove
144:   a Java CDI bean can mount them.
145: 
146: ## App DX
147: 
148: ```java
149: @ApplicationScoped
150: public class MyApp {
151:     @Produces @Singleton PathlandApp main() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); }
152:     @Produces @Singleton MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); }
153: }
154: ```
155: 
156: ## Verified by
157: 
158: Manual: the `pathland-quarkus-demo` renders `/` (the music player, whose Now
159: Playing pane embeds the small `/ad` app via a **same-server `ProxyView`**,
160: spec/PROXY.md) and `/ad` (the ad app); a WebSocket handshake to `/_pathland/ws`
161: and `/ad/_pathland/ws` returns 101. `ProxyDemoTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts
162: `GET /` embeds the `/ad` app's subtree with remapped node ids
163: (`data-pathland-id="1073741825"` — proxy block 0 + origin id 1). Core behavior is
164: covered by `pathland-server-core` tests. `MultiSessionWebSocketTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) opens **100 concurrent real WS
165: sessions** against `/_pathland/ws` (via the shared `pathland-server-core` test-jar
166: probe) and asserts each connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level PONGs, stays isolated,
167: and is never closed by the peer.
168: `PathlandObservabilityTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts `/q/health` reports the Pathland
169: check UP and `/q/metrics` exposes the `pathland.*` namespace. `BaseCssTest`
170: (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts the linked SSR `<link>`, the immutable `text/css`
171: response at the global and mounted bases, and a 404 for an unknown hash.

24: # never appears in the URL. Off by default; the worker is served at /_pathland/sw.js
25: # with Service-Worker-Allowed: / (root scope) and no-cache.
26: pathland.service-worker=true
27: 
28: # The DOM client bundle ships in the Quarkus extension jar (`META-INF/resources`)
29: # and is served by Quarkus's static handler. The demo's media/icons are served
30: # from a disk extraction via DemoAssetsRoute, which sends its own caching headers.
31: quarkus.http.static-resources.max-age=168h
32: 
33: # Pathland SSR debug comments: when true, every rendered HTML node is prefixed
34: # with a comment naming its component type and the modifiers applied, e.g.
35: #   <!-- #1 VStack: spacing=4, alignment=Fill -->
36: # Debugging aid — opt-in; the live /ws deltas are unaffected.
37: # pathland.debug-html=true
38: 
39: # --- Observability (issue #62) -------------------------------------------------
40: # Structured (JSON) console logging — the production-shaped reference app default.
41: quarkus.log.console.json.enabled=true
42: # Metrics: Micrometer counters/timers at pathland.* are exposed at /q/metrics
43: # (Prometheus); health at /q/health (smallrye-health). See pathland-server-core.
44: #
45: # OpenTelemetry spans per frame send / event batch are OPT-IN. The starter wires the
46: # tracing decorator automatically when a Tracer is available, so to enable them just
47: # add the extension and point it at a collector:
48: #   <dependency>io.quarkus:quarkus-opentelemetry</dependency>
49: #   quarkus.otel.exporter.otlp.traces.endpoint=http://localhost:4317
50: # (the extension is intentionally NOT a dependency here, so local dev is quiet).
51: 
52: # --- SEO document head (issue #45) --------------------------------------------
53: # Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are emitted by default; the app can refine them
54: # per route via PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...).
55: pathland.seo.site-name=Pathland Music
56: pathland.seo.og-type=website
57: pathland.seo.structured-data=true

content.text:
Here's what I found, then a prioritized set of ideas grounded in what the runtime already tracks.

## What's already exposed (baseline)
- `/q/health` (mounts + active sessions) via `PathlandHealthCheck`
- `/q/metrics` with the `pathland.*` catalog via `MicrometerTelemetry`
- `PathlandSignalHub` as a CDI bean, but only `subscriberCount(topic, subject)` — no enumeration
- Config flags (`pathland.debug-html`, `pathland.service-worker`, `pathland.seo.*`)
- No Dev UI hooks today; `pathland-quarkus-deployment` only contributes security defaults, native resources, and build items.

## High-value, Pathland-specific pages

**1. Opcode / wire inspector (the killer feature)**
Pathland's differentiator is the 16-byte opcode stream, and nothing currently surfaces it. A dev-only bounded ring recording outbound batches + inbound events, decoded into `Category | Command | Flags | A | B | C` plus arena strings, with a live timeline. Show per-batch: frames coalesced, opcode count, bytes, merge/encode time, sequence number, coalescing ratio. This makes `DeltaBatcher`, `FrameCodec`, and the "zero opcodes when unchanged" property visible and debuggable.

**2. Live session inspector**
A table of sessions per mount: `uiId`, `wid`/state scope, active route, viewport, connected age, last sequence, batches/opcodes/bytes, tree node count, subscriptions, proxies. Actions: force `META::RESYNC`, close session, open in a tab, set color scheme. This directly targets the multi-window isolation and reconnect bugs called out in `status.md`.

**3. SSR vs live preview**
Render a route through `registry.renderHtml(route)` and compare it with the live session tree/DOM; toggle `pathland.debug-html` node comments. Pathland's "SSR renders defaults, live session re-syncs persisted state" split is subtle and a frequent source of "why did it flicker" confusion.

**4. Reactive / tree inspector**
Snapshot the retained tree (component type, id, text, properties, bound signals) on the actor and show which nodes/signals an update touched. A counter for "updates that emitted zero opcodes" is a great demonstration of the fine-grained emitter.

**5. Protocol catalog (build-time page)**
`spec/protocol.tsv` (349 lines) is perfect Dev UI material: searchable primitives/modifiers/events/properties, plus a "decode an opcode" playground and links to conformance vectors. Free documentation inside the tool, and useful to expose via MCP.

**6. Topic hub console**
Group subscriptions by `(topic, subject)` with counts; publish a test payload to live sessions; show `published/coalesced/dropped`. Needs a read-only snapshot API on `PathlandSignalHub`.

**7. Persisted-state inspector**
In-memory `StateStore` keys/scopes, inspect/reset a `wid` scope, and "simulate reload" (new session, same `wid`). Requires key enumeration, ideally dev-only.

**8. Proxy topology (for the BFF/proxy story)**
Show `PROXY_VIEW` nodes → origin endpoint, id block range, connection state, snapshot latency, reconnects, dropped batches. Very useful given `spec/PROXY.md` complexity.

**9. Theme / token workbench**
Effective token set (app overrides vs renderer defaults), force `platform/light/dark` live, reset theme, and show the resolved `base-<hash>.css` / DOM bundle hashes.

**10. Dev MCP tools**
Quarkus 3.39 supports exposing JSON-RPC Dev UI methods as MCP tools (`mcpEnabledByDefault`). Read-only tools (list sessions, describe session, decode batch, get SSR HTML, protocol lookup) plus a few explicit actions (resync, navigate, publish topic). This gives coding agents eyes into a running app.

## Core changes this requires (read-only, dev-only)
- `PathlandRegistry`: a `sessions()`/`snapshot()` view (the map is private today, line 78).
- `PathlandSession`: read accessors for route, state scope, viewport, connection state, root id, tree/subscription/proxy snapshot; DTO built on the actor thread.
- `SessionSubscriptions.snapshot()` + `PathlandSignalHub.subscriptions()` (currently only `subscriberCount`).
- A dev-only bounded trace seam (a `PathlandTelemetry` decorator or a `PathlandDevTrace` no-op SPI) to capture opcodes/batches without adding a production dependency.
- Optional dev-only enumeration on `InMemoryStateStore`.
- Ship `spec/protocol.tsv` as a build-time resource (keep it generated from Rust; add a drift check in tests/CI).

## Implementation shape
- `pathland-quarkus-deployment`: a `PathlandDevUiProcessor` (`onlyIf = IsDevelopment`) producing `CardPageBuildItem` pages and build-time data; add `quarkus-devui-deployment-spi`.
- `pathland-quarkus` runtime: a `dev.pathland.quarkus.devui.PathlandDevUiRpc` bean with `@JsonRpcDescription` methods, registered via `JsonRPCProvidersBuildItem`; rich pages as `qwc-*` web components or `ExternalPageBuilder` endpoints.
- Keep everything under `dev.pathland.quarkus.devui`, never native, never on the production path.
- Tests: JSON-RPC unit tests against a fake host + a `@QuarkusTest` dev-mode smoke test.

## Suggested phases
1. **M1**: Overview card + sessions table + resync/close + build/asset info (needs session snapshot API).
2. **M2**: Opcode/wire inspector + SSR preview + protocol catalog (needs dev trace + `protocol.tsv`).
3. **M3**: Topics console, state inspector, proxy topology, theme workbench, reactive/tree inspector.
4. **M4**: Dev MCP tools.

# Pathland Quarkus Dev UI — full plan, M1 first

## 0. Branch & sequencing
Start from the current clean `main` (`2a1c2281`, matching `origin/main`):

```
git switch -c feat/quarkus-dev-ui
```

One feature branch, one commit per milestone (repo style is `feat(quarkus): …`):
- M1 `feat(quarkus): add Dev UI shell and live session inspector`
- M2 `feat(quarkus): add opcode trace, SSR preview, protocol catalog`
- M3 `feat(quarkus): add topics, state, proxy, theme and tree inspectors`
- M4 `feat(quarkus): expose Dev UI tools over Dev MCP`

Every milestone updates `pathland-quarkus/status.md` and `pathland-server-core/status.md`.

## 1. Design rules
- Dev UI is **local-dev only** (`IsLocalDevelopment`), never registered in prod/native.
- Server core exposes **immutable read-only snapshots**; no renderer state, no business-state retention.
- Reads of actor-confined state happen **on the registry actor**; actions call existing public APIs only (`resync`, `close`, `setColorScheme`, `publish`).
- Bounded buffers, best-effort callbacks, zero cost when Dev UI is absent.
- No new JNA/Lettuce/native dependencies.

## 2. Module layout
```
pathland-quarkus-deployment/
  .../PathlandDevUiProcessor.java          // CardPageBuildItem + JsonRPCProvidersBuildItem
  src/main/resources/dev-ui/qwc-pathland-*.js
pathland-quarkus/
  .../devui/PathlandDevUiRpc.java          // @JsonRpcDescription runtime methods
pathland-server-core/
  .../introspection/*.java                 // immutable snapshot records
  .../PathlandDevTrace.java                // M2 seam (NOOP default)
```
Add `quarkus-devui-deployment-spi` to `pathland-quarkus-deployment/pom.xml`. Quarkus 3.39 provides `CardPageBuildItem`, `Page.webComponentPageBuilder()`, `JsonRPCProvidersBuildItem`, and Lit/Vaadin `qwc-*` pages with `JsonRpc`/`.onNext` streaming.

---

## 3. M1 — Dev UI shell + live session inspector (detailed)

### 3.1 Core introspection API (`pathland-server-core`)
- `PathlandSession`: store `sessionId`, `openedAtMillis`, runtime `theme`/`colorScheme`; add atomics for `inboundEvents`, `resyncs`, `lastActivityMillis`.
- `PathlandSession.snapshot()` (actor-confined) returns `SessionSnapshot`:
  - `id`, `mount`, `stateScope`, `route`, `viewportWidth/Height`, `connected`, `closed`, `rootId`, `treeNodes`, `openedAtMillis`, `lastActivityMillis`, `subscriptions`, `proxyCount`, `stats`
  - `route` from `activePath.get()` on the actor
  - `treeNodes` from a new `Emitter.treeSize()`
  - `subscriptions` from a new `SessionSubscriptions.snapshot()`
  - `proxyCount` from `proxyHost.activeProxies()` (0 when null)
  - `stats` from `DeltaBatcher.snapshot()` + session atomics
- `DeltaBatcher.snapshot()`: synchronized `batchesFlushed`, `lastFrames`, `lastOpcodes`, `lastBytes`, `sequence` (add counters; no prod telemetry changes).
- `PathlandRegistry.snapshot(timeout)`: submit to the actor (reuse the `onActor` guard from `shutdown`) → `RegistrySnapshot(mount, base, debugHtml, serviceWorker, activeSessions, sessions)`.
- `PathlandHost.snapshot()` → `HostSnapshot(running, totalSessions, mounts)`.
- Make `PathlandAssets.bundleName()`/`bundleIntegrity()` publicly readable (or add a small `PathlandBuildInfo` facade); CSS hash already comes from `HtmlRenderer.baseCssName()`.
- Tests for snapshot correctness and actor safety (reuse `RegistryConcurrencyTest` style).

### 3.2 Quarkus Dev UI
- `PathlandDevUiProcessor` (deployment):
  - `@BuildStep(onlyIf = IsLocalDevelopment.class)` → `CardPageBuildItem`:
    - card texts: mount/session counts, flags, version
    - card actions: Open app `/`, Health `/q/health`, Metrics `/q/metrics`
    - page: `Page.webComponentPageBuilder().title("Sessions").icon("font-awesome-solid:window-restore").componentLink("qwc-pathland-sessions.js")`
  - `@BuildStep(onlyIf = IsLocalDevelopment.class)` → `new JsonRPCProvidersBuildItem(PathlandDevUiRpc.class)` (Dev UI registers it unremovable).
- `PathlandDevUiRpc` (runtime, `dev.pathland.quarkus.devui`):
  - injects `PathlandHost` + config
  - `@JsonRpcDescription` methods: `overview()`, `sessions()`, `resync(sessionId)`, `resyncAll()`, `closeSession(sessionId)`
  - `@JsonRpcUsage(Usage.DEV_UI)` for M1
  - returns records/maps, never leaks `PathlandSession`; actions return `{ok, error}` instead of throwing
- `qwc-pathland-sessions.js`:
  - LitElement + `@vaadin/grid`, `JsonRpc`
  - columns: mount, session, route, state scope, connected, age, viewport, batches/opcodes/bytes, sequence, subscriptions, proxies, tree nodes
  - auto-refresh (2s) + manual refresh; per-row resync/close; empty/error states
- No new runtime deps (`JsonRpcDescription` comes from Quarkus core); only the deployment SPI dependency is new.

### 3.3 M1 acceptance
- `mvn -pl pathland-server-core,pathland-quarkus,pathland-quarkus-deployment -am test` passes.
- `cd lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo && mvn quarkus:dev` → `/q/dev-ui` shows the Pathland card; Sessions lists root `/ad` and `/kotlin` sessions as they connect; resync/close work; closing a tab removes the row.
- `mvn package` → Dev UI absent, `/q/health` + `/q/metrics` unchanged.
- Status files updated.

---

## 4. M2 — Opcode trace, SSR preview, protocol catalog
- Add `PathlandDevTrace` (public core interface, `NOOP` default), threaded host → registry → session:
  - `batchSent(sessionId, mount, sequence, bytes)`, `eventsReceived(sessionId, mount, events)`, `ssrRendered(mount, route, nanos, bytes)`, `sessionOpened/Closed`.
- Dev-only bounded ring (1–2k entries, drop-oldest) in the Quarkus runtime; decode outbound batches with `FrameCodec.decodeFrame`; never throw.
- RPC: `trace()`, `clearTrace()`, `streamTrace()` using a Mutiny `BroadcastProcessor` with `onOverflow().drop()`; Dev UI uses `.onNext`.
- **Wire page**: timeline + filters by mount/session/category; opcode table (`category | command | flags | A | B | C` + decoded string operands for known ops); batch size, coalescing ratio, sequence, hex copy.
- **SSR preview page**: route input → `registry.renderHtml(route)` → iframe `srcdoc` + source toggle; “open live app”; optional debug-comment render via a dev-only override.
- **Protocol catalog page**: build-time data from `protocol.tsv`; search primitives/modifiers/events/properties; opcode decode playground. Ship the TSV as a `pathland-view-core` resource (Maven copy) with a drift test against `spec/protocol.tsv`, or copy it into the deployment jar.
- Tests: ring bounds/drop-oldest, known-batch decode, protocol resource drift, RPC serialization.

## 5. M3 — Topics, state, proxies, theme, tree
- **Topics**: `PathlandSignalHub.subscriptions()` snapshot; `publishRaw(topic, subject, value)`; UI grouped by `(topic, subject)` with subscriber counts, publish dialog, published/coalesced/dropped.
- **State**: `DebugStateStore` (`keys()`, `get()`) implemented by `InMemoryStateStore`; UI lists `name:scope`, filters by `wid`, delete/reset, “simulate reload”; graceful fallback for Redis. Inspection only on the actor.
- **Proxies**: `ProxySession.snapshot()` (`proxyId`, `block`, `endpoint`, `ready`, `snapshotReceived`, `attempts`, `originRootId`); `ProxyHost.snapshots()`; topology table + reconnect count + “request origin snapshot”.
- **Theme**: store `theme`/`colorScheme` on `PathlandSession`; show app overrides vs renderer defaults (ship `design/build/manifest.json` if needed); actions `PLATFORM/LIGHT/DARK`, reset theme; show CSS/DOM bundle hashes.
- **Tree inspector**: `Emitter.snapshotTree()` on the actor → immutable node DTO (id, component name via `Components`/protocol catalog, text, property keys, bound flags, children); node selection, id copy, “zero opcodes when unchanged” counter.
- Tests per feature.

## 6. M4 — Dev MCP
- Mark read-only methods `@JsonRpcUsage(Usage.devUIandDevMCP)` + `@DevMCPEnableByDefault`.
- Tools: `listSessions`, `describeSession`, `recentBatches`, `decodeBatch`, `getSsrHtml`, `searchProtocol`, `listTopics`; actions `resyncSession`, `navigateSession`, `publishTopic` behind `pathland.dev-ui.allow-actions`.
- Optional build-time `@DevMcpBuildTimeTool` for protocol lookup.
- Tests: usage discovery; MCP actions off by default; docs.

## 7. Cross-cutting risks
- **Actor safety**: snapshot on actor with a timeout; never read signals off-actor.
- **Dev UI JS**: Lit/Vaadin provided by Dev UI; keep the JS small, no bundler.
- **Classloading**: JS in deployment resources; runtime RPC class registered only in dev; verify prod/native exclusion.
- **Cardinality**: never add topics/subjects to Micrometer tags.
- **Security**: local-dev only; document `quarkus.http.host` exposure; gate MCP actions.
- **Protocol drift**: TSV copy checked in CI like `ProtocolManifestTest`.
- **PII**: state inspector is dev-only.

## 8. Verification matrix
- Unit: snapshots, RPC, trace ring, protocol resource.
- Integration: `@QuarkusTest` or plain JUnit with a real `PathlandHost` + `InMemoryStateStore`.
- Manual: demo dev mode, two tabs, `/ad` proxy, `/kotlin`.
- Prod: `mvn package`, run jar → `/q/dev-ui` absent; health/metrics unchanged.
- Optional: GraalVM Dockerfile build.

## 9. Defaults I’ll take unless you object
- Branch `feat/quarkus-dev-ui`.
- M1 actions: resync single/all + close session only.
- M1 UI: one Sessions page + default card (no custom card component).
- `protocol.tsv` shipped in `pathland-view-core` (M2).
- Dev UI actions on by default; MCP actions opt-in (M4).
- No prod build items, no new production dependencies.

I can’t create the branch or edit files while plan mode is active. Approve/exit plan mode and I’ll create `feat/quarkus-dev-ui` and execute M1 as specified.

  Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding
  effects, structural reconciliation, fit/media/navigation routing, and the
  zero-opcode unchanged recompute contract. A replaced child is relinked to its
  real parent (not the tree root), so a `SIZE_THAT_FITS` swap cannot detach a
  pinned root `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` or drop its media routing. Registered `MediaController`s are
  projected as pinned, non-visual root children; `unregisterMediaController`
  removes them without touching the app tree.

## Implemented

- **Dev UI (M1)** — the extension registers a **Pathland** card in the Quarkus Dev
  UI (local development only). A **Sessions** page lists every live session per
  mount (route, state scope, connection state, viewport, age,
  batches/opcodes/bytes/sequence, subscriptions, proxies, retained tree size) and
  offers resync (single/all) and close actions; the card links to the running app,
  `/q/health`, and `/q/metrics`, and shows a live app/session summary. Backed by
  read-only `PathlandHost`/`PathlandRegistry`/`PathlandSession` snapshots and the
  dev-only `PathlandDevUiRpc` (`overview`, `sessions`, `resync`, `resyncAll`,
  `closeSession`), registered via `JsonRPCProvidersBuildItem`. Both build steps
  are gated by `IsLocalDevelopment`, so production/native builds carry no card,
  component JS, or Dev UI bean. Verified in dev mode (the component is served at
  `/q/dev-ui/pathland-quarkus/qwc-pathland-sessions.js` and
  `pathland-quarkus_sessions` returns live sessions) and in a packaged prod app
  (`/q/dev-ui` is 404; health/metrics unchanged).

  scope, viewport, connected/closed, retained tree size, proxy count, topic
  subscriptions (topic/subject/pending), and inbound/resync/batch counters.
  `DeltaBatcher.stats()` supplies batch/opcode/byte/sequence counters,
  `Emitter.treeSize()` the node count, `SessionSubscriptions.snapshot()` the
  subscription list, and `PathlandBuildInfo` the DOM bundle name/integrity. No
  mutable session/tree internals leak; a snapshot that cannot reach the actor
  fails fast instead of reading actor-confined state off-thread.

content.text:
M1 is implemented on `feat/quarkus-dev-ui`.

**Added**
- Read-only snapshots in `pathland-server-core`: `PathlandHost.snapshot()`, `PathlandRegistry.snapshot()` (runs on the actor), `PathlandSession.snapshot()`, plus `DeltaBatcher.stats()`, `Emitter.treeSize()`, `SessionSubscriptions.snapshot()`, and `PathlandBuildInfo`.
- Dev UI processor: `PathlandDevUiProcessor` with a Pathland card + Sessions page + Open app/Health/Metrics actions.
- Runtime RPC: `PathlandDevUiRpc` (`overview`, `sessions`, `overviewSummary`, `sessionsLabel`, `resync`, `resyncAll`, `closeSession`).
- Sessions web component: `qwc-pathland-sessions.js` (live grid, auto-refresh, resync/close actions).
- Tests: `PathlandIntrospectionTest`, `PathlandDevUiRpcTest`.
- Updated `pathland-quarkus`, `pathland-server-core`, and `pathland-view-core` status docs.

**Verified**
- Full tests pass: `mvn -pl pathland-server-core,pathland-quarkus,pathland-quarkus-deployment -am test`.
- Dev mode: card/component registered; `pathland-quarkus_sessions` returned a live session (route, viewport, 306 tree nodes, 1 proxy, stats).
- Packaged prod app: `/q/dev-ui` 404; `/q/health` and `/q/metrics` unchanged.

Changes are uncommitted on the branch. Want me to commit M1 (`feat(quarkus): add Dev UI shell and live session inspector`) and then start M2?
Hw do I try it out?

From the repo root, install the changed JVM modules once, then run the demo in dev mode:

```bash
cd lib/java
./mvnw -pl pathland-server-core,pathland-quarkus,pathland-quarkus-deployment -am -DskipTests install

cd pathland-quarkus-demo
../mvnw quarkus:dev          # add -Dquarkus.http.port=8081 if 8080 is busy
```

Then open:

- **Dev UI:** http://localhost:8080/q/dev-ui → the **Pathland** card → **Sessions**
- **App:** http://localhost:8080/ (also try http://localhost:8080/kotlin)

Notes:
- The Sessions list only shows **live** sessions. Open the app in one or more tabs; the page auto-refreshes every 2s. Each tab gets its own session (`wid` is per window).
- The music player embeds `/ad` via a proxy, so you should see `proxyCount: 1`; `/kotlin` adds another mounted app.
- Interact with the app (click buttons, etc.) to watch `batches / opcodes / bytes / seq` update.
- **Resync** sends `META::RESYNC`; **Close** drops the server session (a live browser client will reconnect and create a fresh one).
- If the card doesn’t appear, you likely ran against stale `~/.m2` jars — rerun the install step above.
- Dev UI is dev-only: a packaged `mvn package && java -jar target/quarkus-app/quarkus-run.jar` serves `/q/dev-ui` as 404.

# Hardening Pathland deployments

Pathland has two distinct security surfaces:

1. **The protocol/client code** (`pathland-core`, `pathland-view-core`,
   `@pathland/dom-renderer`) — malformed opcodes must never panic, over-allocate,
   or execute markup/script. These bounds are fixed in code and covered by tests;
   reporting guidance lives in [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md).
2. **The HTTP/WebSocket host** — origin checks, response headers, message-size
   limits, and rate limiting. These are framework/deployment concerns and are
   configured through Quarkus or Spring Boot.

This guide is Quarkus-first (the primary server target) with a Spring Boot
appendix.

## Pathland defaults never override your configuration

Pathland contributes framework defaults only, never programmatic overrides:

- **Quarkus** uses `RunTimeConfigurationDefaultBuildItem`, which becomes a
  lowest-priority `DefaultValuesConfigSource` (ordinal `Integer.MIN_VALUE`).
  `application.properties`, profile-specific files, environment variables, and
  system properties all win.
- **Spring Boot** contributes `server.forward-headers-strategy=framework` through
  a lowest-precedence `EnvironmentPostProcessor` property source. An explicit
  strategy in your configuration wins.

Adding Pathland can still change behavior when a setting was previously **unset**
(that is what a default is): CORS, forwarded-header trust, WebSocket caps, and
the baseline security headers. All are listed above and every one can be
overridden with normal application configuration.

## What Pathland does not use

- **No session cookie.** The per-window state scope (`wid`) lives in
  `sessionStorage` and is sent only on the WebSocket query string (and, when
  enabled, attached to navigations by the service worker). There is therefore no
  cookie to mark `HttpOnly`/`Secure`/`SameSite`.
- **No CSRF token.** SSR is read-only (`GET`), and the only state-changing
  channel is the WebSocket. WebSocket CSRF is prevented by the origin check
  below (browsers always send `Origin` on a WebSocket handshake).

## Quarkus (secure by default)

The `pathland-quarkus` extension contributes these runtime defaults via
`RunTimeConfigurationDefaultBuildItem`; application configuration always wins.

```properties
quarkus.http.cors.enabled=true
quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding=true
quarkus.http.proxy.allow-x-forwarded=true
quarkus.http.proxy.enable-forwarded-host=true
quarkus.websockets-next.server.max-message-size=65536
quarkus.websockets-next.server.max-frame-size=65536
quarkus.http.header."Content-Security-Policy".value=default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; media-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' ws: wss:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; worker-src 'self'
quarkus.http.header."X-Content-Type-Options".value=nosniff
quarkus.http.header."Referrer-Policy".value=no-referrer
quarkus.http.header."X-Frame-Options".value=DENY
```

### WebSocket origin / CSRF

Quarkus's CORS filter runs before every route, including WebSocket upgrades.
With `cors.enabled=true` and **no `origins` configured**, it allows same-origin
requests only (missing `Origin` is allowed — non-browser clients). This is the
WebSocket CSRF control.

If browsers must connect from another origin, list them explicitly:

```properties
quarkus.http.cors.origins=https://app.example.com,https://staging.example.com
```

Never use `quarkus.http.cors.origins=*` for a stateful Pathland app. Quarkus has
one global CORS policy, so this also applies to non-WebSocket HTTP endpoints:
list any legitimate cross-origin API consumers, or set
`quarkus.http.cors.enabled=false` and enforce the origin check in your own
gateway/filter.

content.text:
Confirmed — it's not your setup. The extension's strict CSP is blocking the Dev UI itself. Headless Chrome shows:

- inline `importmap` blocked: `script-src 'self'`
- `https://fonts.googleapis.com/...` blocked: `style-src`
- `data:` fonts blocked: `font-src`
- then `Failed to resolve module specifier "lit"` → the SPA never boots, leaving the blue "Quarkus" splash.

### Quick workaround (try it now)
Add this to `lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/src/main/resources/application.properties` and restart the IntelliJ `quarkus:dev` run:

```properties
%dev.quarkus.http.header."Content-Security-Policy".value=default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; img-src 'self' data:; media-src 'self'; font-src 'self' data: https://fonts.gstatic.com; connect-src 'self' ws: wss:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; worker-src 'self' blob:
```

Then reload `/q/dev-ui/` (hard reload is safest). The Pathland card and Sessions page should appear.

### Proper fix (recommended)
Don't contribute the CSP default in **local dev**; keep the strict CSP in test/prod. In `PathlandProcessor`:
- remove the CSP entry from `securityDefaults()`
- add a non-dev-only build step:
  ```java
  @BuildStep(onlyIfNot = IsDevelopment.class)
  RunTimeConfigurationDefaultBuildItem contentSecurityPolicy() {
      return new RunTimeConfigurationDefaultBuildItem(CSP_KEY, DEFAULT_CSP);
  }
  ```
This mirrors Quarkus: the Dev UI is incompatible with a strict CSP, and dev mode isn't the production security surface. Apps can still set their own CSP in dev if they want.

Also update `docs/HARDENING.md` to say the CSP default applies to test/prod, and add the dev-mode note to `pathland-quarkus/status.md`. `SecurityHeadersTest` stays as-is because test mode remains strict.

Want me to implement the dev-only CSP fix and verify the Dev UI boots with headless Chrome?

`RunTimeConfigurationDefaultBuildItem`; application configuration always wins.

```properties

quarkus.http.header."X-Content-Type-Options".value=nosniff
quarkus.http.header."Referrer-Policy".value=no-referrer
quarkus.http.header."X-Frame-Options".value=DENY
```

### WebSocket origin / CSRF

Quarkus's CORS filter runs before every route, including WebSocket upgrades.
With `cors.enabled=true` and **no `origins` configured**, it allows same-origin
requests only (missing `Origin` is allowed — non-browser clients). This is the
WebSocket CSRF control.

If browsers must connect from another origin, list them explicitly:

```properties
quarkus.http.cors.origins=https://app.example.com,https://staging.example.com
```

Never use `quarkus.http.cors.origins=*` for a stateful Pathland app. Quarkus has
one global CORS policy, so this also applies to non-WebSocket HTTP endpoints:
list any legitimate cross-origin API consumers, or set
`quarkus.http.cors.enabled=false` and enforce the origin check in your own
gateway/filter.

### CSP

The default policy allows same-origin scripts only. Inline **styles** are
unavoidable because the protocol emits `style` attributes and
`<style data-pathland-tokens>` / `data-pathland-fit` blocks, so `style-src`
includes `'unsafe-inline'`; scripts do not.

Override the policy (or relax it while rolling out) with application config:

```properties
quarkus.http.header."Content-Security-Policy".value=default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; ...
```

For an initial rollout you can use `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only`
instead. Do not add `'unsafe-eval'` or `'unsafe-inline'` to `script-src`.

### HSTS (whole-origin, app-owned)

HSTS is intentionally **not** an extension default. Unlike the per-response
headers above, it pins the **entire origin** in the browser: every path and port
(and every subdomain with `includeSubDomains`), including other apps served by
the same Quarkus instance. It also outlives the Pathland app. A reusable
extension cannot know the deployment's TLS topology, so the application (or its
edge proxy) must opt in.

For a hosted, HTTPS-only app:

```

omits it: the Quarkus Dev UI is served there and its inline import map, inline
bootstrap scripts, and Google Fonts are incompatible with a strict script CSP.
An application can still set its own CSP in dev if it needs to test one.

The demo `application.properties` is unchanged — the quick CSP workaround is no longer needed. Changes remain uncommitted on `feat/quarkus-dev-ui`.

input.newString:
- **Dev UI (M1)** — the extension registers a **Pathland** card in the Quarkus Dev
  UI (local development only). A **Sessions** page lists every live session per
  mount (route, state scope, connection state, viewport, age,
  batches/opcodes/bytes/sequence, subscriptions, proxies, retained tree size) and
  offers resync (single/all) and close actions; the card links to the running app,
  `/q/health`, and `/q/metrics`, and shows a live app/session summary. Backed by
  read-only `PathlandHost`/`PathlandRegistry`/`PathlandSession` snapshots and the
  dev-only `PathlandDevUiRpc` (`overview`, `sessions`, `resync`, `resyncAll`,
  `closeSession`), registered via `JsonRPCProvidersBuildItem`. Both build steps
  are gated by `IsLocalDevelopment`, so production/native builds carry no card,
  component JS, or Dev UI bean. Verified in dev mode (the component is served at
  `/q/dev-ui/pathland-quarkus/qwc-pathland-sessions.js` and
  `pathland-quarkus_sessions` returns live sessions) and in a packaged prod app
  (`/q/dev-ui` is 404; health/metrics unchanged).
- **Dev UI (M2)** — a bounded `PathlandDevTraceStore` (1,000 entries, oldest
  dropped) is installed as the `PathlandDevTrace` only in local development and
  registered as an unremovable bean by the deployment module. It decodes outbound
  batches (`FrameCodec`) into category/command/flags/A/B/C plus the `SET_TEXT`
  string operand, and records inbound events, SSR renders, and session lifecycle.
  Three pages: **Wire** polls `trace(sinceId, limit)` (newest-first timeline,
  kind/session filters, an opcode detail view, clear), **SSR** renders a mount +
  route through `registry.renderHtml` into a script-disabled iframe (source
  toggle), and **Protocol** browses the bundled `protocol.tsv` via build-time
  data with kind/search filters. `clearTrace` keeps the id high-water mark so a
  polling client never re-fetches.
